independence: Independent source challenge of visible root conclusions; not cleanroom. All scenarios source-derived/unexecuted.
anchors: source-key:one-based-line; exact file and hash in sources

findings.claim: poll can paint after context/logout/alive changes during response.text await
findings.witness: Fetch resolves in old admitted context; text() stays pending; body context key changes, region disconnects, or logout attribute becomes true; text resolves before next timer tick and without owner.stop(). stopped=false and sequence unchanged, so onResponse is called with stale body.
findings.prerequisites: The context change occurs AFTER post-fetch revalidation and BEFORE body promise resolves. No tick/explicit stop/rescan cleanup may stop controller or supersede sequence first. Actual delivery requires a deliverPollResponse hook; default bootstrap onResponse only optional-calls internals.deliver.
findings.counterevidence: poll:157-175 validates all conditions each tick;204/235 stopped/sequence drops obsolete responses;210-220 checks logout/alive/context after fetch. Explicit stop sets stopped and aborts; next tick invalidation prevents this witness. Therefore do not claim arbitrary context changes always paint.
findings.correction: Core and bootstrap wiring have a body-await admission window. Visibility is checked at tick only, not after fetch or body; a hidden transition without a tick likewise remains possible, but root requested context/logout/alive.
findings.required_control: Re-prove current authorization/context/alive/visibility immediately after body await and before onResponse, preserving stopped/sequence checks and stop reasons; no new polling policy selected.

findings.claim: SubmitFetch adapter abort does not physically abort request
findings.verdict: supported; logical supersession and physical one-inflight differ
findings.witness: First SubmitFetch promise remains pending through cadence tick. Adapter abort rejects wrapper only; next tick invokes a second SubmitFetch with method GET, headers{}, no signal. Both underlying requests can remain active even while first logical result is suppressed.
findings.prerequisites: Injected fetch cannot independently abort from another owner signal. To demonstrate physical overlap it must remain active past cadence. No transport probes performed.
findings.counterevidence: Abort-before-entry prevents invoking fetch. Promise first settlement rejects on abort, and later physical resolution cannot re-resolve wrapper. Sequence/stopped guards suppress late logical results. Custom PollFetch can accept signal; claim must be scoped to submitFetchPollFetch/boot adapter.
findings.correction: One logically admitted current response is enforced; physical one-inflight is not established by adapter. Aborted never-settling underlying promise retains its resolution closures; listener removal occurs on physical settlement271/275 (once abort listener has fired it is removed by once semantics). Core sets inflight=null207 before text, so controller ownership also ends before body reading; no assertion that stop cancels body after headers.
findings.required_control: Either carry an actual signal into transport contract or explicitly qualify logical cancellation and physical concurrency/resource budget. This packet chooses no interface policy.

findings.claim: initial binder throw strands global/element leases
findings.verdict: supported partial initialization; categorical unrecoverability unsupported
findings.witness: Replace a known scanned binder via registerBinder; initial rescan binds an earlier poll region then later known binder throws. Global listeners/hook are already acquired, live map already set, and collected earlier stop handles are not unwound; startBrowserClient throws before returning handle.
findings.prerequisites: Only poll-region/guarded-form/once-action selectors are scanned. A new arbitrary registered id is not sufficient. Throwing custom binder/DOM adapter/hook is permitted by structural API but ordinary core happy path does not throw here. Failed binder-owned partial acquisitions cannot be cleaned by host if no stop handle was returned.
findings.counterevidence: LIVE_CLIENTS WeakMap returns the partially initialized client on next start299, so caller can retrieve and invoke stop if its disposers work. WeakMap is weak, not by itself a permanent memory leak. Initial entry failure is therefore recoverable in some paths; known nonthrowing DOM/core setup succeeds.
findings.correction: Say acquired leases lack automatic failure unwind, not permanently unreachable. Hook registration can also throw before live map set (374), leaving global listeners without map retrieval; scope each failure position separately.
findings.required_control: Initialization unwind must dispose already-acquired handles/remove listeners/map registration, preserving primary failure. Each binder owns cleanup before a failed return.

findings.claim: throwing stop hook strands later cleanup and prevents retry
findings.witness: onHtmxSwap returns a release function that throws. stop sets stopped=true then calls it358; hash/key listeners, bound stop handles and map deletion366 are skipped. Second stop returns at354; start again returns same stopped client299. Alternatively one entry.stop throws363 and later entries/map deletion remain.
findings.prerequisites: A user-supplied release/registered known binder disposer or structural remove listener throws. No throw is required from ordinary native DOM listener removal.
findings.counterevidence: PollRegion.stop itself marks stopped, clears timer, aborts inflight BEFORE optional onStop125-128; onStop throwing alone does not leave that poller's timer active. Bootstrap may still fail to clean other regions. Normal nonthrowing cleanup is terminal and complete.
findings.correction: Separate PollRegion resource cleanup from BrowserClient multi-lease cleanup. rescan348 can also throw before bound.splice349 and leave later stale handles. Do not claim every stop throws or all leases survive a failing entry.
findings.required_control: Attempt every independent cleanup and delete/clear owner registration in total finally paths; preserve/report original cleanup failure without making second stop silently certify release.

findings.claim: diffReportValues throw skips table row scope.dispose
findings.verdict: supported exceptional-cleanup hole; ordinary comparison/domain qualification matters
findings.witness: Scope acquired; setup/invoke/observe resolve. observe returns an object whose enumerable x getter throws when compared against {x:1}; comparator exception at equal57 escapes both executeRow catches and await223, so dispose225 is never called and sequential runTable rejects before later rows. Rejection before/after snapshot comparison147 has the same hole.
findings.prerequisites: Getter/proxy witness is outside the advertised JSON-safe plain report-value intent; it proves robustness to unexpected harness errors, not a valid authored report mismatch. A sufficiently deep finite recursive report tree can instead exhaust recursive comparison stack; no supported depth/threshold was measured, so do not assert an exact minimal depth or executed stack failure. Actual physical leak requires scope owns disposable resources.
findings.counterevidence: Setup, snapshots, invocation and observe errors are caught and returned, then normal runOneRow disposes. Ordinary plain finite shallow values return mismatch arrays rather than throwing. Disposal failures are already reported as isolation-unproven226. tabletest170 tests normal per-row disposal, not this uncovered exceptional comparator path.
findings.correction: Failure is cleanup skipped on uncaught execution error, not every mismatch leaking scope. Unexpected comparator/harness errors need no new language admission decision to require acquired-scope finally cleanup.
findings.required_control: Wrap acquired-scope lifetime around all executeRow paths with finally disposal; preserve primary unexpected failure and disposal diagnostics. Comparator domain/depth policy remains separately qualified.

limits: No tests/builds/runtime/network/Git/repo edits/new JEV/policy/acceptance. Source tests only identify scenario coverage, not fresh execution. No claim about broader browser owner adapters or testkit scope substrates beyond inspected callable APIs.
